situation: I hate my job but I am scared to quit and seek a new career.

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.content: I am having a lot of anxiety about quitting my current job. It is too stressful but pays well

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: What makes your job stressful for you?

dialog.content: I have to deal with many people in hard financial situations and it is upsetting

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Do you help your clients to make it to a better financial situation?

dialog.content: I do, but often they are not going to get back to what they want. Many people are going to lose their home when safeguards are lifted

dialog.content: But you offer them a better future than what they have currently. It may not be what they wanted, but it helps them in the long run.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I can understand that.

dialog.content: Is there another job that would pay you close to what you currently make?

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Is it possible to reframe how you look at your clients' dire financial situations?

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is also true. Sometimes I wonder if it really is for me though

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I've had to deal with collections before when I was in  bad financial condition. The person on the other line was really helpful though. She was understanding,

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It may not be for you. I think you should think about the pros and cons of keeping your position. It might make things clearer for you.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is true. Maybe I just need to sit down and really think about it

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I wouldn't stay if it really impacts your mental health in a negative way. Still, you may need to zoom out and see the bigger picture: that you provide a needed service and you do it compassionately

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It really is a big decision

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you for the different perspective

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is true. Thanks again

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Bye

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It's no problem. I hope you can make a decision about this situation and then be at peace with it

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ok, take care

situation: I have been out of work for five weeks in quarantine due to testing positive for COVID-19.  I fear that my employer will not take me back to work even once I test negative.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hi there, how are you feeling today?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hello

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hi :) Is there anything you'd like to talk about? Something on your mind?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm concerned about my job. I have been out of work for the past 5 weeks because I tested positive for COVID-19.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Oh I am so sorry to hear that! Are you at least getting sick pay? If not, are you getting advice about help you might be able to access?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Oh I am so sorry to hear that! Are you at least getting sick pay? If not, are you getting advice about help you might be able to access?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: (sorry for duplication, not sure what happened there!)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It just keeps getting better...  I applied for the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance and was approved.  The next day, I got an email asking me to verify my identity (I am fine with that.  It actually makes good sense.)...

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: So you have been getting some assistance?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: So I did as instructed and got the message on the website thanking me for verification.  The following week I got a physical letter saying I was approved and the award amount per week.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have gone online once a week and qualified, as one is supposed to do, and still I have not received a cent.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I see, so you are really financially struggling at the moment? Is there anywhere else you could apply for assistance? What about a foodbank?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Calling the customer service line is futile.  The computer just plays a recording that the agents are on other calls and then it disconnects the call.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hear you there - I spent a long time on hold for an official matter the other day. I guess that everyone is really desperate for help and advice right now.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have been very fortunate.  People in my church have been bringing me food.  I plan on trying to go to the food bank Monday, if they are open.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hope that they can help you. My partner and I have used one before and they were very helpful. I felt a bit ashamed but there was no judgement at all.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I actually got so tired of redialing the Department of Labor and Training that I sent an email to the Lieutenant Governor of the state asking for his assistance in getting the matter resolved.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That sounds like a very positive thing to have done. I really hope that they pay some attention to you. This situation is not your fault!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have been to this food bank once before, and they actually made me feel very comfortable and welcomed and gave me an information package on other ways the parent organization may be able to assist me.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yes they are run by lovely people. Ours gave us a pamphlet for cheap and easy to make recipes too.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I am very lucky in that the organization is only 3 miles from me.  I will be looking into their rent assistance and employment assistance programs as well.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: So, at least it sounds like you have a good handle on this and are doing everything you can to help yourself, am I right?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have an advantage because I have a professional background in cooking, so I can take random ingredients and turn them into wonderful and nutritious meals.  I just need to have the ingredients.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That sounds very encouraging! It's amazing what you can make even with cheap food. Noodles , for instance, are very versatile :)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: You are right.  I am definitely not going to sit and pout.  I am just a bit frustrated with the system.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It's a very strange situation and I suspect that some of the authorities just feel overwhelmed and have no idea how to cope.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I am concerned that my boss may try to not take me back at my job.  Because this is an "at will" state, he can terminate me without cause.  Although he can not legally fire me for being ill with COVID, he can take me back and simply release me the same day saying that I have become redundant.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That would be incredibly immoral of him. Do you feel that he is likely to do such a  thing?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I would not put it past him.  Sadly.  But I have taken the attitude that if it does occur, there is nothing I can do to change the situation.  I would simply pursue a charge against him for wrongful termination, and seek a new job.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That is a very rational way to look at things. I really hope that it does not come to thank though! Thank you for talking and I wish you all the best for the coming months.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I may not win the suit, but I would definitely file one.  In 2000, I had an employer fire me without cause.  I sued and won that time.  Not only did they have to pay me back wages for the 90 days that the investigation took place, which was no minor sum,

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am glad that you'd not roll over and accept ill treatment! Well done :)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: they were found to be guilty, so the judge granted me my wages based on the average of 80 hour weeks I had been working, all my vacation time, plus the overtime I would have received, holiday pay, and then to put a nice bow on that gift, he awarded me 5000 dollars in damages because the old company lied and said I had broken the law.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am afraid I need to leave now but thank you for talking :) (can you press the quit button and take the survey?) Best wishes!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My current employer actually knows this happened, because years ago we discussed it, and I showed him the award letter from the Department of Labor and Training, itemizing the judge's findings and the awards.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you for your time.  Have a great holiday.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You too!

situation: My ex partner is harassing me and will not stop talking to my friends and family.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hello

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hi! How are you today?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have been better

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It sounds like you might be upset. Can you tell me what’s going on?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My ex partner and I broke up a long time ago because they cheated on me. Now they will not stop contacting my friends and family and posting about me on social media

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That sounds difficult and stressful. What do you do when you see it happening?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I usually just document it and try to not go online for a while. It is hard to ignore

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It sounds like you are avoiding things you enjoy because of their actions. I think documenting it is a good idea! Have you tried reporting them for harassing you?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have tried but everyone just tells me there is nothing they can do because they don't think it is dangerous or criminal at this point

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That must be very frustrating. Can you tell me if you’ve tried other things to get them to stop?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have confronted them in person but it was dramatic to say the least. They basically had a meltdown that they don't want to lose me

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You tried to do the right thing and they are having a difficult time letting go. The ongoing comments through social media sounds like they are wanting your attention. That can be exhausting for you. In my past, I had to block someone who did something similar to me. If my friends mentioned seeing something from my ex about me, I asked them to keep it to themselves or consider blocking them,too. The people who were closest to me understood what was going on and I realized that people who didn’t know me, didn’t matter. Would you be willing to suggest this to friends or family if it would help to remove the ex from your interactions?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have encouraged my friends to block them as well, but a new account always pops up. My ex really will not give up.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I see. How long has this been going on and is this a daily occurrence or does it happen at certain times?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It has been happening for at least 6 months now and it usually happens every weekend

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I can sense your frustration. It must be overwhelming at times and make you dread the weekends. It sounds like it has become a habit for your ex. It might help if you write a letter to them explaining that you are ready to move on and are asking them to do the same. Explain that you are giving them the opportunity to stop harassing you in the following ways [list some of the details you have documented]. Inform them that if they do not stop, you are considering taking it further regarding harassing communications and that this letter serves as your intention to no longer tolerate their actions. Send it via certified mail and keep a copy. This will give them no way to immediately respond and would be the first step of official documentation should they decide to continue.  Do you think that might help?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I think that is an excellent idea! That is a good way to end this once and for all.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I sincerely hope it is a step toward you regaining your control  over how you are able to interact with people. I wish you the best in dealing with this and hope you begin to feel better about it soon, especially entering into a new year!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you very much!

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I joined just over ten years ago.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My church is my anchor.

dialog.content: I imagine he is missing his big sister

dialog.content: If you mean me, I'm male.

dialog.content: The Lord is using you to each others/

dialog.content: At the end of the service, she found me and gave me a big hug around my legs and then looked up and said "I always wanted to go to a church where someone knew MY language!"

dialog.content: God placed you there for that little girl

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: From that point on, there was no problem with me signing in church.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I think He placed her there for me, also.  It was a mutual deal.

dialog.content: You have a calling on your life. Don't let the dream die

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: He will use you in mighty ways

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Well... I should be going, but thank you for taking the time to chat.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ok. Hope I was of help

dialog.content: I am a Christian also

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content:
You definitely were.  I am feeling better than I have in about a mo
nth.  I appreciate that.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: God put you here tonight for a reason

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: God loves you.

dialog.content: Of this I have no doubt.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Glad  iI was here.

She has taken from me all parts of my job that I value.  This upsets me personally and I am sad & angry that the rest of my team, who I care about, is no longer supported.  We have no recourse to solve this problem.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hello there, how is life treating you at the moment?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Not too bad outside of work.  I'm miserable there.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: So you are experiencing problems at work? Please tell me about it, I am happy to listen.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Things have changed and my new supervisor has crushed my spirit by taking all the parts I love away.  She never liked me and now she gets to make me suffer.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am very sorry to hear that - trouble with workmates, especially those who are in a higher position, can make things very miserable can't they?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: They really can.  I used to love my job and my team.  Now she has made everyone miserable because she just doesn't care about learning the job or the job at all.  My morale is low and worse because I can't help my peers who are struggling as well.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Have you considered going over her head and putting in a complaint? Especially if she is making everyone else miserable as well. Someone more senior might be able to do something.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have considered this many times.  Unfortunately, the next level manager doesn't respect or value my team in general.  She has made that clear.  She's also just awful and uncomfortable to talk to.  I've found her to just be mean sometimes.  It just feels so hopeless.  Just waiting for someone to notice.  Just hoping she fails.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It's just really hard to show up everyday.  But I do.  Although the days are long and exhausting with no motivation to perform.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Please try to stay positive - bullies never prosper in the long term. I think that you need to talk to your co-workers about this and see if you can come to some sort of arrangement between you

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Alternatively, have you ever considered seeking another job? I know that that might feel like selling out but you might be happier somewhere else

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: You are right.  She is a bully.  I have called her several names to myself, but not a bully yet.  My coworkers and I have discussed what options we may have.  My suggestion was that we work at our normal pace rather than scrambling to make up for her failures.  I wouldn't want to set her up, but I think her failing is the only way we will ever see a solution.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have applied for another job within my company.  There seems to be interest in me, so that's exciting.  It is a job I really want.  But then, of course, I feel bad about leaving my peers behind.  I really care about them.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I feel that that is fair enough. You should not be working to make up for her failures and I hear you saying that you feel that this is w hat is happening?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Definitely. Everyone is struggling.  I am the one my team expects to help with some of the tasks she is not performing.  I'm happy to do it for my team, but there is no recognition.  But I think I have been giving them good advice about hanging in there, staying positive, etc...  I should probably listen to myself.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: (sorry was afk give me a second to catch up :))

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I really feel that you have grounds for a formal complaint. Just her being incapable is bad enough but bullying too is unacceptable

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: You may be right.  My company has an anonymous reporting system.  I should learn a little more about how that works and see if that's an option.  I'm not sure things could get much worse at this point.  This could be my last ditch effort.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's good advice and you saying it directly to me makes me think I should lean into it.  I can't just spin my wheels in misery much longer.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Anonymous reporting sounds like a good thing, as long as it's not being abused. This sounds like a very good time to use it though

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hope I have been able to give you some good advice here!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Most definitely. I feel more confident now about the anonymous reporting.  I'll gather some notes from my peers to ensure I have a viable complaint.  That's so helpful.  Thank you.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You are most welcome, enjoy your day!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Are you saying that he has cheated on you before? That does not sound very promising.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: He has but it was a long time ago and was before we had a talk about exclusivity in our relationship but it still hurt.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Have you considered getting some sort of couples counselling? Or do you just think that he is never going to change?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: We tried counselling once.. It was online and we got paid to do it.. I don't think he took it seriously at the time. He always said he felt like he was being attacked.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am sorry to hear that. So you feel that he is not really taking your problems as a couple seriously?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes. I feel he thinks of me as some sort of trophy and he does not have to work now that he won me over in the first place.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I have been in toxic relationships before and to be honest it does sound a little as though this is one of those situations.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have been as well but this time was supposed to be different. At first everything was great but now things are so distant I just don't know what to do next.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Do you feel that perhaps it might be time to move on? People who will cheat twice are pretty unlikely to ever change their ways.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is true. But now we have a kid together and I feel like it would break her heart to lose her dad

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ah you did not mention that! Maybe for the sake of your child it might be worth going to counselling again then.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Maybe but a place that we won't get paid to go... I think he thought of it as a job or something. I got a lot out of the experience and still use the skills to this day. But with a unresponsive partner those skills will not work.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Can you recomend a good site to find affordable services?

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: They should be able to provide you with a list of reputable services local to you .

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hope that I have managed to be of some use to you today!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: absolutely best advice I have gotten in a while. It was nice talking to you.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Nice talking to you too, enjoy your day!

situation: My boss reduced my pay so that he gets a bonus

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hi

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hello though, how has life been treating you lately?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It's been a pretty crazy year. I'm mostly bummed because of my work.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It has been a really weird year hasn't it? Don't worry, I think it's been the same for all of us. Would you like to tell me more details?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Sure, when covid hit my company did a round of layoffs and also cut everyone else's pay by 10%... I was bummed but I kind of understood because I knew our business would be impacted by closures. I found out recently that my boss (the VP) is intentionally making our impact seem worse so he can keep our salaries reduced and overall cost lower so that he can get a higher bonus next year.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That really sucks! I can understand why you are angry and anxious about this and you have every right to be!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Are there any official routes that you can use to complain?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I work in supply chain and I see the actual sales numbers and realized 4 months ago that we were actually on track to exceed our plans, even with the covid reductions. a few weeks later I heard him tell our sales director to keep the numbers artificially low so that they will both get their bonuses

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I don't think so... He's the VP there isn't anyone I can go to above him

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That is genuinely unfair. Have you looked into getting free - or low cost at least - advice about making a formal complaint?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It really should not be legal for your boss to be taking advantage of workers like this

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I don't know if it is or not... I used my EAP benefit through work where you can talk to a councilor for free (5 visits) and they said that it's unfortunate but they didn't think it was illegal.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am very sorry to hear that, that sounds extremely unfair to me. Have you considered looking for another job? I realise it's a very difficult time to be looking for work right now though

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: yeah, it's tough.. I don't know if anyone is hiring. because of the timing like you mentioned.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I've looked a little bit though

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I really can't wait for this year to be over! It's been so awful. Do you suppose anyone at all has had a good year?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: haha I don't know... I'm sure someone has... heck the VP is getting a Bonus... so I'm sure he'd say he's having a good year

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Well yes fair point! Us poorer people are not doing very well though!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Have you tried to talk with any of your coworkers about this? I would suggest that it might help.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Amen.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's a good call, I've got a work buddy who I feel somewhat comfortable talking with. I may try and reach out to him

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I really think you should. You have a legitimate grievance and being able to discuss it with people who understand might help a lot.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I feel a little guilty about sharing what I know because I almost feel like ignorance is bliss at this point. But then I feel guilty for keeping that info

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I feel that people have the right to know what is being done and will be happy you told them.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I agree and I think you're right. I appreciate you chatting with me about this

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You are very welcome. I hope I have been able to be of some help to you and you will continue to talk to other people about it.

situation: I am extremely stressed with work and am very unhappy.

dialog.content: Hi how are you?

dialog.content: Im not doing very well at all.

dialog.content: What's going on?

dialog.content: I am a lab assistant.

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you! I will try that.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: no problem!

situation: I have this overwhelming fear and pressure that my mother will not be accepting of my grades in school. This pressure has caused me to feel anxiety everyday and perfect all homework assignments which I do not have time for.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes, I am feeling very anxious about my school work lately.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I see, so your main worry is about academic pressure?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Is there a specific aspect that you are focusing on?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes, I am focusing on my grades and the pressure I feel from my mom.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Have you been performing below your normal standard this year?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: she wants me to get all A's. I feel she has too high of expectations sometimes, which makes me feel like I need to perfect my assignments and spend all this time on them.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: No, I do well, it just causes me a great amount of stress.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hear you, I have been in a similar situation. Parents sometimes do not realise just how much pressure they are putting on their children to be perfect.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I feel like as long as I am meeting the requirements and am passing, she should be proud of my accomplishments.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: She should be proud I am even going to college.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Exactly! there is nothing at all wrong with not being a straight A student.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Have you tried to tell her how you feel about her behaviour and attitude towards your studies?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Exactly. I feel like there is this society stereotype of needing straight A's otherwise you are a failure or something.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: A bit, but she uses the "I pay for your education" card.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Which makes sense, but still, I know I am doing well so it's just a lot at times.

dialog.content: Absolutely not. There is nothing wrong with not being perfect. And she has no right to emotionally manipulate you by mentioning money.

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's what I keep telling myself, but I have this overarching fear that I will be in debt forever then.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Debt is a very scary thing to experience, I know. I do worry a lot about it sometimes too so you are not alone.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That makes me feel better.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: The main thing is, do you enjoy your studies and consider them worthwhile?

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.content: S

dialog.content: Are you able to confide in your friends about your situation and your worries?

dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I have dealt with depression around this time of the year since i was 17.  I am now 37.  My cousin got killed in a car accident on Dec 29th  at the age of 14.  Then 18 years later on Jan 3rd I lost my boyfriend in a car accident.  I struggle around the holidays even worse now than I  did before.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hi there, how are you?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I am doing ok.  How are you?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I'm doing well, thanks for asking. What are you seeking support for today?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have been struggling for motivation to do anything the past couple weeks.  This is a really hard time of year for me.  I lost my cousin in a car accident at the age of 14 in a car accident coming up on 20 years this year.  We were very close.  I was 17 at the time.  Her was an alcoholic and my parents raised her a majority of her life.  Then 3 years ago 5 days after her death anniversary I lost my boyfriend at the age of 32 in a car accident.  I dread the holidays.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Thank you for sharing that. It sounds like you are describing a strong association between the holiday season and loss of loved ones. This leads to less of a desire to engage in typical holiday events. Does that sound right?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: You are exactly right.  The year my cousin got killed her mom was hungover so I went and picked up my cousin and her little brother to take them to our grandparents house for Christmas dinner.  She died 4 days later on Dec 29th.  And my boyfriend it was his first day back to work after the New Year.  He died on Jan 3rd.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I usually go all out for the holidays to try to hide my depression every year.  This year I just can't bring myself to enjoy them.  I have even bought one christmas present.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I can see why this time of year is difficult for you. Trying to hide depression can be a challenge. Rather than hiding the sadness or grieving feelings, some people find relief in acknowledging and sharing these feelings with family members who may relate. Do you ever share these feelings with your cousin or grandparents that you mentioned?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My cousin doesn't live around here and we have never been real close.  He is alot younger than me.  We just never had the connection like his sister and I did.  And both my grandparents have passed away.  Grandpa has been gone for 12 years and Grandma has been gone for 4 now.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My family has always been really good about talking about our loses. Things just will never be the same.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I understand. When losses are experienced it is a great change in many aspects of our lives.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Are there any aspects of the holidays that bring you joy? Maybe holiday music, movies, bright snow (if there is snow where you live), or seeing joy on someone's face when you give them a great gift?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: They say it gets easier. And I agree it does.  Things just have changed so much.  I miss how life was before I lost them.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I understand - and it is normal to feel that way. When we lose someone who brought us happiness, it is only natural to miss them and their company.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I love giving gifts.  And I always put lots of thought into the gifts I give.  My nieces and nephews can't wait every year to see what I got them.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That's great! You must have a special talent for personalizing your gift selections. Perhaps focus on that reaction from you nieces and nephews to support your motivation for giving gifts this year.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: This year I am tie dying hooded sweatshirts.  I make tshirts for a hobby.  And to tell you the truth thats the only gifts I have gotten so far.  My oldest daughter turned 18 this year and lives with her boyfriend so its just me and my 15 year old daughter.  She struggles with depression/anxiety as well.  Her dad has been in jail for some stupid actions since August.  She has had to deal with him being an addict pretty much her whole life.  I think we are both missing how the holidays were with her sister still living at home.  Too much change in our lives in such a little time frame.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Wow, what a great gift idea! That is a solid start on your gifts for the season, and something to be proud of.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: They will love them.  A couple years ago I put their names on fleece blankets when I worked at an embroidery shop.  They absolutly loved them!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: And I see, it sounds like the changes in your life are potentially impacting your daughter as well. However, I'm glad you have each other for support this season. This year has been crazy for many reasons, and many people tend to find comfort in routines or traditions. Do you and your daughters have any holiday traditions you typically complete?

dialog.content: Awesome gift idea! Personalized gifts are always so heartfelt and appreciated. Good thinking!

dialog.content: Just the normal traditions.  My oldest daughter will be here for Christmas morming.  Then we go to my parents.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you for chatting with me tonight!  I hope you have a good rest of your night.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I find that when I have a very painful situation, I try to only thing about it for a certain amount of time. Then I make a list of things to do so I can be occupied to not think about it.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Getting over a breakup will take time? Have you ever heard of DABDA? Denial (I can't believe this happened!) Anger (we all know that) Bargaining (If only I had done that, or if only - trying to make it FEEL better by imagining other scenarios - doesn't really work) Depression - sadness, then Acceptance -- we go in and out of these emotions and sometimes it can make us feel crazy, but all of them are normal in varying degrees and we don't know when they will happen.

dialog.content: I would make a list of things you have always wanted to do and then just BRAINSTORM any idea, no idea is too out there -- learn to ice skate, learn to play the ukulele, sign up for dance lessons, join the gym, go to a singles group at church, visit the elderly, volunteer somewhere.

dialog.content: I think I need to focus on exercise. Just get my body and mind healthy and full of energy. What do you think?

dialog.content: I also find it helpful not only to limit how much I dwell on my pain, but make sure I reach out to help someone else. I will tell you, that is the secret to happiness. dialog.content: True, but it's hard not to dwell. It's not like I have a choice. It overcomes me.

dialog.content: I agree, get healthy and try to help others. dialog.content: Hmm. But what if I spend the fee to get my resume looked at  but then don't land a job? Wouldn't it be better to save the money and hedge my bets?

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.content: Perhaps you should speak to a trusted mentor or a closed loved one and seek their opinion. Often, we need someone outside of the actual situation that can give us great advice.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Also, there are many online resources that are great at finding available jobs and require your time and effort, but not any money invested. This might be a good tool as well!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hope so. I've also been in a similar situation so I can completely understand your feelings.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Keep in mind there are also resume sites that are free to use, as I know you are concerned about the financial part in that area.

dialog.speaker: seeker

situation: Nothing special just an ongoing thing i've been dealing with since my daughter was born.

dialog.content: I've been dealing with a lot of depression lately.  not sure how to shake it (1)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My daughter was born about 3 months ago.  I guess it's post-partum.(2)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Well I figured when I was crying at the Pampers commercial that there might be an issue (3)

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.content: Yeah, I'm not big on the medication.  I've talked to several moms that went on it and years later had to stay on it because the withdrawals were so terrible.  I'd like to be able to process through it(7)

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: And whats the worst a little talking can do for you. Has talking to other moms been helpful at all?

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yeah its a rough cycle, you get down on yourself for feeling down.

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.content: Very true.  Thanks for reminding me.  I think I worry more about the outcome than I need too.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Don't forget to breathe. Exams are stressful but I would suggest don't cram everything to the last minute. Usually the hour before the exam, I do something else.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Very good advice.  Any suggestions on what I can do?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Stay calm, believe in yourself, start your studying early so you are not cramming everything in the last few days.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Great Advice.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: But, in the one hour prior to the exam, do you have any advice on something I can do to calm my nerves?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Walk outside, away from the students waiting for their tests.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Wonderful suggestion

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you for your help.  I think I will go walk now.  Best regards.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Is there anything else I can help you with?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: No.  Thank you.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Goodnight and good luck.

situation: I'm frustrated with Covid, having family issues, and I'm the caregiver for my disabled sister. Plus the holidays have been cancelled and so I'm just pretty anxious and depressed.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hi.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm anxious and depressed.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Is anyone there?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: im here

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hi. I'm anxious and a bit depressed.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: what made you feel this way?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: The pressures of Covid and taking care of my disabled sister are just getting to me.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: i see how that could make you a bit anxious. I get the same way also.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thanks. I'm just tired of the Covid restrictions. I can't wait for things to get back to normal.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: i feel the same. being on lockdown could make anyone a little crazy

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: do you have family or friends that you could reach out to over the phone?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I do. My other sister is always a big help. Maybe I should text her more often?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: yes! that would always be a good idea. its always comforting to hear from a loved one.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: i myself yearn for a good call from family or even hearing someone close voice. always makes me smile.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's true. I tend to stew on my thoughts.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: hows the weather where you are?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It's not too bad. Cloudy and 40 which is pretty good for this time of year. How's your weather?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: i live in the south . not cold yet. but your weather sounds like it would be nice for a lovely walk.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Exercise does always help. I walk/jog five miles every day. I generally feel my best right after that. Don't you find that true too?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: yes! although i probably couldnt walk nor run 5 miles a day. i love getting out to enjoy nature. it always helps to keep mind off things. does that usually work for you?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes, I love nature but I live in a congested suburb. It would take me awhile to get out to the country. That's why Covid is so tough - I can't travel which is my main form of relaxation. What do you do to relax?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: i see, for me to relax. i find sitting back in my recliner reading a nice book always relaxes me. i also love yoga. its a refreshing relaxtion

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I should try yoga. I sometimes do breathing exercises when I get really stressed. Maybe I should go back to it. What do you think?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: actually that would be a good idea. i find yoga and breathing deep help relieve stress & let go of the negative.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I think I'll try it. Thanks! It was good talking to you. I think we completed the requirements. Have a good Thanksgiving and stay safe out there. Bye!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: you too always :-)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thanks!

situation: Everything was going crazy in the world with COVID. I was worried about my daughter and her education. Then suddenly, I lose a lot of my hours at work and have to quit one of my jobs due to the virus and becoming her main caretaker again. This really makes me nervous because the price of everything is continually going up and I have little excess money to spend.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hi, not a good time right now. Really concerned

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I'm sorry to hear that . How can I help?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I just need someone to listen. I want to know everything will be ok

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I really hope things get better sooner than later

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I understand. Tell me what's going on.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I'm here to listen.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Since CORONA I have had to quit working my second job and become a full time stay at home parent. This is causing our family a loss of considerable income and with everything going on right now in the world it makes it even more worse.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I understand. It is a scary time right now. Things will not always be this way though. We will get through it.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: The important part right now is to stay safe and healthy for yourself and for your family.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: What kind of work did you do before the pandemic?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'd like to think this will be over sooner than later, but it's hard to really think about it. I was a merchandiser for retail stores.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I had been a stay at home parent before so our family was used to one income for a long time. It was nice to not always have to stress about money since I was working again. It seems the stress is a lot more now though because of everything going on in the country.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yes our country is in a lot of uncertainty right now. And having a second income always helps. Have you considered possibly finding a work from home job? Perhaps look at what skills you've developed, and update your resume to reflect the skills you have that will transfer over to a work from home job.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm always concerned about scams. There are so many untrustworthy places that I hate putting myself and my information out for others to get who aren't honest.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I understand. There are always companies or jobs out there that are scams. What I found worked best was looking at reputable sites like LinkedIn, GlassDoor, etc. Right now is a good time to find a work from home job from reputable companies. I've found that a lot of companies have transitioned over and developed jobs that can be done from home. I actually work from home myself.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Oh thats really encouraging. I will definitely look into that.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Another suggestion I can make is contacting your local workforce department  (department of unemployment) as they can make suggestions too.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I never thought about the unemployment office. I know so many people are worse off than me that I almost feel guilty to reach out. I really appreciateyour trips

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: tips

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You already have a lot of skills you didn't think about. As a stay at home parent, you are like the CEO of your own company. You manage day to day operations. You also do scheduling, finance management, etc.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's very true!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I understand feeling guilty for asking for help.  But don't worry that is what they are there for!

seeker_question1: It really helped me speak to someone I didn't know who wasn't going to judge me.

situation: co workers seem to ignore me and don't say hello, i feel unwanted

situation: I just got layed off.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hi. How are you doing today?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I can't believe it I just got layed off.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I'm sorry to hear that. It is a tough time right now for people working. Do you want to talk about it more?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I know. It's going to be nearly impossible to find something good now.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I understand that it is frustrating and scary to lose a job. But depending on what field you work in, there are actually quite a few places hiring right now because of the holidays.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: My boyfriend was laid off from his job and was able to get interviews with a handful of places in his area. Granted, they are not dream jobs, but at least it is a paycheck.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I live in a small town. The mill is pretty much all we have that pays good.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Do you have access to any areas outside your town that are in driving distance or a bus can reach?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have my car. No bus's go through here.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Well if you have a car, maybe you would be able to find something a little outside your area that would pay more. Try taking a look on indeed.com or even craigslist for open positions. You may be surprised by what you find and a change in career can sometimes be a positive thing

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I just got out of the Air Force. I really need a steady paycheck right now.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: The only way you are going to be able to get a job is by looking what is out there. If you can work retail, it is a great time for that because of the holidays. Even if it is a temp position, at least it is something.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: And the holidays are just about here. This is going to suck.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It is a difficult time in general for a lot of people. I think most people are going to be understanding this year when it comes to gift giving. I wouldn't worry too much about that and instead focus on what you are able to do about the situation.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: This is the first time in 3 years i will be home for Christmas I was hoping to make for not being here.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Perhaps think of you just being home as the gift. Having time to spend with your family and friends is likely to mean more than something you can buy.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My luck we won't be able to leave the house.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Then make it a great experience in the house. Make decorations and do holiday things. There is a lot people can do this time of year without going outside that is fun and meaningful. Try to be optimistic even in tough times. Sometimes it is all we can do to get by.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I was thinking about learning how to make my own beer. Two birds one stone.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yeah! That is a great idea. I know people that started doing that and ended up opening their own local brewery. You never know what could happen when you try new things!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is true.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hope I have been a little helpful for you today. It is tough right now but we can get through it.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you and have a great weekend.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You as well.

situation: I'm mad at my boyfriend for not taking responsibility.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hello

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hi, how are you?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Good thanks, so what's troubling you?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm so mad at my boyfriend for not taking any responsibility.  I'm about to break up with him.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Responsibility in regards to what?  Like in what area of life do you mean?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: We've been dating 4 years, meeting in high school.  Now we're graduated and I've gone to college.  He doesn't have a job yet after 1 year.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hmm, has he been looking for work, or just laying around playing video games and shit like that?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I've been away at college and just came home on break so I'm not sure.  He tells me he is looking but I don't know how it's taking a year to get a job.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Well, I suppose it's possible that he's been earnestly looking and just not having any luck.  Is he kind of a loser in general, or is he a stand-up guy?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: He got average grades in school but didn't really miss days from school.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ok, so it sounds like you're kind of fed up with him in general, and not having a job is maybe just a part of the bigger issue?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's probably correct.  He hasn't been in contact with me as much since I left for school.  I just expected more.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Well,  it sounds like you're both in kind of a transitional period in life.  It's pretty normal for relationships to not necessarily survive through things like this

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's so sad since we have so many years together, but I feel like I'm moving forward and he is staying in place.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yeah, I mean it's never easy going through a breakup, but people change as they get older and mature, and they aren't necessarily going to still be compatible the whole time.   Also I think it's important to not think of a relationship that peters out as a failed one.   Just because it didn't last until one of you died doesn't mean it wasn't a success.   I think people put too much emphasis on permanence.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's true, it can maybe just be a stepping stone to build other relationships.  Thanks for the wisdom.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Well I've got a couple decades on you, so I've been through this a few times before.   Actually I'm still friends with pretty much all of my exes.   I mean just because I'm not romantically involved with them anymore doesn't mean that they aren't still terrific people.   Hell, I hung out with two of them just today.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's great you have maintained positive relationships and were also able to move  forward.  Thanks for the advice. I appreciate it.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You bet.   So what do you think you'll do from here?   I mean do you know you want to move on for sure, or do you think you'll see if you can work through this patch?  I don't know that there's a wrong answer .

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm going to spend some time thinking about it some more but won't regret if my choice is to move on.

supporter_question1: It was a pretty good conversation

dialog.content: not leaving the house is the new normal for many of us right now. are you not leaving because you have nowhere to go or because you are feeling bad

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: you havve already made it two weeks by going one day at a time

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I did not really have any choice though .  I do not see any future for myself now that we are separated.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: do you know brene brown and her work

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: No I do not, who is that?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: she studies vuneraility and shame. please look for her TED talk and there's a great youtube video on empathy

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you , I will. Right now I really need some sort of emotional support. I feel that the last fifteen years of my life have been a waste.

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: a relationship is part of who you are. it isn't you

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: But it is very difficult to try to strike out on my own again and I do not know if I even want to.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: it is hard. it sucks. but the voyage through the suck is going to be better for you than you may realize right now

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: But I feel that I am facing middle age on my own and I really do not want to do that.

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I feel I might have missed out on my chance to have a family of my own though, because I waited fifteen years and my partner would not go for that.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: please watch the cartoon animals and brene brown on youtube talk about empathy. find one of your friends who has been through the suck and let them help you find your path out.

dialog.content: Most of my friends seem to be very happily coupled up right now. They are sympathetic but they do not really understand.

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: stay strong and stay safe

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hmm... So have you two live together?  How long has this kind of behavior persisted? When you ask her about this behavior, how do you present the question and how does she react? Finally, how often do you talk with her about the situation?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: very true. I suppose I have just assumed at this stage with no real evidence. do you think I should just talk to her?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Forgive me if this comes off as disrespectful... I only want to help you.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: not at all. I appreciate your candour.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: But if you feel as though you're a joke regardless, then why stay in a relationship where you're getting hurt? I know that you don't want to lose the beauty but would you not be happier with loyalty?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content:
All this is tied up with who and I know I'm valuing the wrong things. You are right actually. I think some of this comes from my low

dialog.content: Yes, that's definitely an expense you can't afford right now. But are you familiar with the concept of controlled breathing to help reduce or relieve anxiety?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Like meditation?

dialog.content: What am I supposed to do? Just breathe in and out a lot?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Not exactly. Controlled breathing is more of getting yourself into a quiet room. Closing your eyes, and purposely and intently focusing on your breathing. dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Oh I didn't know that. No, I haven't tried that. Does it really work?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: One exercise I find helpful is lying on my back with a pillow under my head. I keep my legs bent and put a pillow under my knees for support. I then put one hand on my chest and one on my diaphram and slowly breathe through my nose feeling my stomach press against my hand. I then exhale slowly through my nose and repeat for about 10 minutes. It can be very calming.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hello every since I lost my job I have felt sad and useless

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That is an extremely tough situation to go through, I'm sorry to hear that.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Application after application I get rejected, it makes it hard to even fill out more

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yes, job applications can feel particularly demeaning to complete.  Personally, I get frustrated with all the repetition and then repetitive rejection.  It seems like I had no value.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: But you have to consider that there are dozens of different reasons why you don't get selected for a job, and quite a few of them have nothing to do with you , either as a person or as an employee.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It feels good someone else knows how frustrating and what a cycle it creates but I am also sorry that you do know how it is also.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you for that, it seems most of the jobs I am applying for I am over qualified for which doesn't make sense to me and makes me think it is something personal about me.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: No, don't think that.  I know of several employers that have actually said they don't want employees smarter than them.  It requires more money and more management, and quite a few people are very happy to not do either of those things for ostensibly higher quality workforce.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: On an actionable level, have you been getting blocked at the application point or the interviewing point?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hopefully I find an employer that sees a quality workforce over other things, its getting pretty discouraging

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I seem to be getting blocked at application level for employment, it seems my skills are mostly being put out to contract work now, which is not something I am familiar with.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I see.  Maybe there are some qualification programs in your local area, or maybe at the local university or college where you could take classes?  There is a career development center at my local university that is open to everyone, maybe you could see if they would review your resume and give you some objective feedback?  Students love a good live subject :-)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Wow I have never thought about that! That sounds awesome and like it would be great help, also trying something new would feel nice instead of filing the same stuff into applications!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You should explore what resources your city/county/province may offer for job seekers.  It is in the best interest of almost every community that its members have have jobs and feel useful, so you may find some valuable information and maybe some connections.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Oh!  And what I always tell everyone who is looking for a job:  Apply UP!  Don't ever think is something above your level.  Apply UP!  They may admire your temerity and invite you for an interview just to see who you think you are :-)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My spirits are going up just having this conversation and looking forward to the community outreach. Hopefully it helps lift this gloom that has been over me for months. I loved my previous job but due to bad management it was taking a toll on everyone employed.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am glad to hear you are feeling a little better!  Yes, bad management is so toxic.  Even with great coworkers in a job you love, horrible management can ruin it quickly.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You seem like you are open to trying new solutions and putting in the effort to up your competitive level.  Stay positive and take care of yourself mentally and physically, and I think you will be successful.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I think that is truly when I started feeling down, productivity was high but it mattered not to those in charge it was never enough.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you so much for talking, I feel so much better already and this was great adivce.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I was in a similar situation, nothing was ever good enough, and we were never given enough information to succeed anyhow.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I am glad to hear that!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm sorry you had to experience something similar by the sounds of it you are no longer in that situation, so that gives me hope for myself!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That is awesome :-)

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: haha yeah!

dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I am at my first semester in a doctoral program and have a lot to do at once and have been feeling very anxious in the past few weeks.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hello

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Good afternoon!  What can I help you with today?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I've been feeling a lot of pressure and stress lately due to school

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Oof, yes, school can be a tough situation.   Are you close to the end of the semester?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That can be both a relief and stressful, because a break is near, but all the exams and projects are due.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes, I am a little more than halfway done with the semester

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: The thing is that I am in a doctoral program, so even though the semester is close to the end, I always need to continue working

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ahh, I see.  That is a great deal of time and work.  What are you studying?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It is... I am in psychology

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have to work on my thesis on the side even with all of my classes and I have a hard time managing my time and keeping track

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Time management can be very difficult with a normal class load, that sounds exhausting.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: It is!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Do calendars help you at all?  I am a super visual person, so calendars and planners are invaluable to me, as well as different colors of ink and labels so I can visually divide my attention

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Getting a million different colors of pens and highlighters changed my organization for the better.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I do keep a physical and electronic agenda, but I feel like even if I write down my tasks, I find a way to procrastinate which is what I am having trouble with

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Also, setting clear boundaries for your study/work and relax times may help.  I like to set a timer for, say, 45 minutes, and work/write/read/study for that long, then, I get a 10 minute break.  I'll go outside, refresh my coffee, grab a snack, dance to some music, stretch, then set another timer for 45 minutes, then another break for 10 minutes.  That allows my brain to take a second and refresh from the work.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is actually very helpful, I'll take note of it

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I think it would help to fix break times so I can actually focus on working

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Or, like, today, I woke up and spent half an hour allowing myself to drink my coffee and scroll through Reddit.  Then it was time to work on my group project for 45 minutes, then a break, then I worked again, took a break, went to a class, etc.  Scheduling your breaks can be helpful too so your lizard brain doesn't freak out and go "WE ARE GOING TO BE WORKING FOREVERRRR"

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I agree!!! That really is helpful, thank you

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: which, for me at least, is where the fatigue sets in.  You're very welcome!  I hope I was helpful.  You seem positive and willing to try new things, and I think you will be successful even if you are tired.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ah, yes, that makes sense. dialog.content: Before you go on, try taking a few deep breaths.  Why not try meditating a few days before?

situation: My girlfriend just told me our relationship isn't working by text. She has recently started a new job and I think she may have met someone else.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: How are you doing today?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm not feeling great. I think my girlfriend may be cheating on me.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: So you think she may, have started a relationship with someone else?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes, I think so although I don't have any proof. Things were going really well and then all of a sudden she text me and told me things aren't working.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ok, well that doesn't sound pleasant and must be difficult to hear. Perhaps her feelings have changed and there isn't necessarily another person involved?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: She has started a new job and I think she might have met someone at work that she likes better than me. I can't believe she is doing this to me!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ok so it seems like you are quite angry at the moment at the thought of her with someone else, is that true?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes I suppose it is true. The thing is I thought things were going well and she is stressed out at work with her new job but we were getting on great!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I had a similar experience myself. My partner was stressed and I was busy myself. It turns out that I wasn't paying him enough attention and this made him feel like I didn't think he was important to me any more.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I haven't thought of it like that before but still I want to talk to her about it not just text me randomly and hint at ending things.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: From my experience, when I actually talked to my boyfriend we agreed to make more time for each other and things did improve.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Okay what do you think I should do about it because the text seemed very final? Looks like she has made her mind up already about things.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Sometimes people say one thing but actually mean another. They are complicated and don't always say what they really mean.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Do you think that she wants to talk rather than end the relationship?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I cannot say for certain however I think you should talk to her but also prepare yourself for the fact that she may actually want to spend some time apart or end  the relationship. it would be wise to prepare for that outcome as upsetting as it may be.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That makes sense but it is not what I want to hear. After all we have been through together, we were even talking about getting our own place together and now all that will be for nothing!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I think you are reflecting on your plans together and the thought of the relationship ending is making you upset and angry.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes that's right. I know getting angry doesn't help but I want things to go back to the way they were.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ok so based on what you have told me I think that your girlfriend has got a new job and you are planning on moving in together is that correct?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes that's right but that's what couples do isn't it?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It is but that is a lot of change all happening at once. Perhaps she is getting a little bit scared and rather than dealing with the situation she is running away, perhaps you should talk about this and see how she responds?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I still think there is someone else that has come between us.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Have you got any evidence of this like seen a text message or has she behaves strangely?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: No I haven't, it is just a feeling.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Ok well it is natural to feel like this sometimes. People tend to fear the worst.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: So do you think I should try and talk to her and ask her outright if she has met someone else?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I think rather than ask her that question directly, you could start the conversation and ask her why she is feeling this way. This would show you care and are prepared to listen without jumping to conclusions.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I think I do need to calm down a bit and maybe talking to her would be the best way to start. I don;t know what I'd do though if she ended it.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: The best thing to do would be prepared to have the conversation, stay calm and listen. She may just want to talk but also be prepared as it may not go the way you plan.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Ok well maybe if I show her that I can stay calm and strong then she will stay with me?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Be prepared that she may end the relationship but getting angry is likely not to change her mind. Getting angry does not improve difficult conversations.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I suppose I could go into it and listen as you have said, there could be other reasons like the new job or maybe morning in that is causing some of it. I'll try and keep calm but it is hard when emotions run high.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Take a deep breath and try to relax beforehand. Staying positive and allowing her to speak will make for a better conversation. She will be more likely to open up to you.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That is actually pretty good advice. I hope we stay together and there is nobody else though.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I hope you manage to work it through and can at least talk about your feelings

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hey thanks for the words of wisdom. Not sure I'll like the chat but I'll try and stay calm.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You are very welcome and take care

situation: I recently found out that my best friend has lied to me about her whole life, and when I invited to my home she finally told me the truth after staying for a month ad we were fighting for the entire month she stayed.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Hello, how are you doing today?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm sad and angry because I no longer talk to my best friend

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Do you know what might have happened to cause your and your best friend to not talk anymore?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Well she was staying at my house for a month and we were constantly fighting so she just stopped talking to me

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That sounds really stressful and I can see how troubling that is for you.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes it is and then she began avoiding me while we were in the same house, so we started arguing again and I found out she's been lying to me since I've known her and I'm very upset.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That's definitely very upsetting. I know how it feels to have that sense of betrayal from a friend I was close to for many years. However, I was able to discuss the issue I had with my parents and other friends. Do you have anyone else close to you that you can talk to?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I don't think so, my parents think I was too harsh by deciding to end the friendship, it as if my own family doesn't understand.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That can definitely add to frustration. What about your other friends? Do you have anyone who either shares the same opinion as you or does not know your friend that you can talk to?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: My other friend believed that it wasn't too harsh to end the friendship as they know I value honesty but it makes me feel angry that I was being used for so long and constantly lied to.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You have every right to be angry, but the most important thing you can do is find a good support system with your other friend. It will take some time to heal, but I'll tell you a paraphrased version of one of my favorite quotes: "Resentment is like swallowing poison and expecting the other person to die." It's important to find support in your other friends and heal properly.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I really love that quote, it's absolutely true; I think I will talk to my friend about the situation some more so I can fully get over it.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Yes, I also realized that I wasn't angry with my friend but rather myself

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Can you elaborate more? Earlier you said you and your friend were arguing while she was living in your house, then she stopped talking to you. Why might you be angry with yourself?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Because I basically allowed her to use me for seven years and kept lying to me or gave her space because I thought I was being a good friend.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I feel like I was stupid to do that and soft

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: If I may, I would argue that your actions don't make you soft and they certainly don't make you stupid. They are certainly not any reason to be angry with yourself. If I may bring up another cliché: "Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me." I would say you're in the "fool me once" stage and it is your friend's actions that have brought you pain. I think you're unlikely to trust her again.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Also, hindsight is 20/20. What you might see now in ways that your friend might have used you are things that you might not have seen then. We want to think the best of our friends until they prove us wrong. I think you were being the best friend you could be.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thank you very much, I'll continue to talk about the issue with my other friend, I really appreciate your wisdom.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Of course. I think you'll be alright and remember the healing process can take a long time after betrayal. Remember to be kind to yourself and keep that support system of your other friend by you.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Is there anything else you would like to discuss?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: No thank you, enjoy the rest of your day

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: You too!
